title: Strategy, Risk Appetite and Business Model Oversight for Boards
summary: An eight-module programme helping boards see their firm the way a supervisor does: testing business model viability, challenging plans and setting risk appetite.
intro: This training programme equips boards and directors to see their firm the way a supervisor does: testing business model viability, challenging the business plan, setting risk appetite and overseeing financial resilience.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give directors the analytical tools supervisors use to judge whether a firm's business model is viable and its strategy sustainable, applied from the boardroom. Participants leave able to challenge management's plans and assumptions, set meaningful risk appetite and evidence effective oversight of strategy to supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: How supervisors analyse business models, business plan challenge, financial resilience, risk appetite statements and limits, stress testing and reverse stress testing, recovery and wind-down planning, M&A and outsourcing decisions, shareholder influence and board independence, and monitoring delivery.
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and members of board risk and audit committees
Chief executives, finance and risk directors and senior managers accountable for strategy and planning
Company secretaries, strategy and planning teams supporting the board
Learning Objectives: Explain how supervisors analyse business model viability and strategy sustainability
Challenge the business plan, its financial projections and key assumptions
Assess financial resilience using profitability, capital, liquidity and concentration measures
Set a risk appetite statement with measurable limits that constrains strategy
Evaluate stress testing, reverse stress testing, recovery and wind-down plans
Oversee major strategic decisions and the delivery of strategy, independent of undue shareholder influence
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies, analytical exercises and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in finance or risk modelling is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)

modules.title: Seeing Your Firm the Way a Supervisor Does
modules.summary: How supervisors analyse corporate strategy and business models, why business model risk sits at the heart of supervisory risk assessment, and what that means for the board.
objectives: Explain what a business model and a corporate strategy are, and how they differ
Describe how supervisors conduct business model analysis and score its outcome
Identify the information supervisors use and how the firm will be judged
syllabus: Business model components, the value chain and key dependencies
Viability over one year and sustainability over three to five years
The supervisory roadmap: preliminary assessment, analysis and scoring
Where business model risk fits in the supervisory risk framework

modules.title: Challenging the Business Plan and Its Assumptions
modules.summary: How boards test the business plan as a supervisor would, from the competitive environment to financial projections, and recognise the patterns behind failed strategies.
objectives: Analyse the firm's macro and competitive environment and its position within it
Challenge financial projections, growth assumptions and execution risk
Recognise why strategies fail and identify key vulnerabilities
syllabus: Environmental and competitive analysis: suppliers, buyers, entrants and substitutes
Testing projections: growth, margins, costs and sensitivities
Execution risk, management capacity and change load
Case study: comparing two contrasting business strategies

modules.title: Financial Resilience and Key Risk Indicators
modules.summary: The quantitative measures supervisors use to judge financial resilience, and how the board uses them to spot vulnerability before it becomes a problem.
objectives: Interpret profitability, capital and liquidity indicators
Assess concentration in income, clients, products, funding and counterparties
Identify early warning signs of business model stress
syllabus: Profitability drivers, cost-income and return on capital
Capital structure, quality and headroom over requirements
Liquidity, funding and concentration risk
Early warning indicators for the board dashboard

modules.title: Risk Appetite Statements and Limits
modules.summary: How to set a risk appetite that genuinely constrains strategy, cascades into limits and triggers, and gives the board a basis for challenge and escalation.
objectives: Evaluate whether the risk appetite statement is linked to strategy and capacity
Set quantitative limits and qualitative statements with escalation triggers
Oversee breaches, cascading and periodic review of appetite
syllabus: Risk capacity, appetite, tolerance and limits
Quantitative and qualitative appetite statements
Cascading appetite into business lines and decisions
FSB principles for an effective risk appetite framework

modules.title: Stress Testing and Reverse Stress Testing
modules.summary: How stress testing reveals how the business model breaks, how to challenge the severity and relevance of scenarios, and how reverse stress testing informs strategy.
objectives: Challenge the design, severity and plausibility of stress scenarios
Interpret results and their implications for capital, liquidity and strategy
Use reverse stress testing to identify what would make the business model fail
syllabus: Scenario design: idiosyncratic, market-wide and combined stresses
Management actions and their credibility under stress
Reverse stress testing: working back from failure
Linking results to risk appetite and the business plan

modules.title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning
modules.summary: Why supervisors expect firms to plan for severe stress and orderly exit, and how the board tests that recovery options and wind-down plans would work in practice.
objectives: Explain the purpose of recovery plans and solvent wind-down planning
Assess recovery indicators, options and their feasibility
Evaluate whether the firm could wind down in an orderly way
syllabus: Recovery indicators, triggers and escalation to the board
Recovery options: capital, liquidity, disposals and cost actions
Wind-down costs, timelines and client asset return
Testing plans through fire drills and playbooks

modules.title: Major Decisions: M&A, Outsourcing and Shareholder Influence
modules.summary: How the board oversees acquisitions, disposals and material outsourcing, and maintains its independence where shareholders or group entities seek to shape strategy.
objectives: Challenge the strategic rationale, due diligence and integration risk of M&A
Assess material outsourcing and intragroup dependency decisions
Maintain board independence and manage conflicts with shareholder interests
syllabus: M&A: rationale, valuation, due diligence and integration
Outsourcing and third-party dependency: oversight and exit
Group strategy, intragroup arrangements and local board duties
Shareholder influence, conflicts and independent judgement

modules.title: Monitoring Delivery and Board Action Plan
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining how boards monitor strategic delivery, respond to unexpected events and prepare for supervisory scrutiny of the business model.
objectives: Specify the management information needed to monitor strategic delivery
Evaluate management responses when strategy goes off track
Produce a board action plan for strategy and business model oversight
syllabus: Tracking delivery: milestones, KPIs and variance against plan
Responding to unexpected events and changing course
Preparing for supervisory business model review
Workshop: assess and score the firm's business model as a supervisor would

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.
